about: Every identifier family in the public tree (release/keep-public.txt) that carries the internal name (BC250 XeFG, XeMFG, bc250-xefg, xemfg), with its current value, where it appears, what renaming it does to existing installations (Restore of their records) and the recommended policy. release/rename.py reads this file: 'scan' lists each occurrence by family (patterns are tried in this order; an earlier family claims a span first), 'apply' rewrites the families it selects with their replacements. Classes: 'user-visible' (apply rewrites those with default true; the others with --family), 'compat' (with --include-compat when they need neither an alias nor a rebuild; otherwise only by --family), 'internal' (never rewritten: an interface, a record value or a build switch; scan lists them), 'review' (the old name left in prose and messages: rewrite by hand). Templates: {name} (the product name), {holder} (the MIT copyright holder: '{name} contributors' unless apply --holder), {slug} (lower case, hyphens), {slug_} (lower case, underscores), {SLUG} (upper case, underscores); \1 refers to a group of the replacement's pattern. 'XeFG', 'XeSS' and 'XeLL' on their own name Intel's software (nominative use) and are no rename item. 'chosen' holds the decided public name (empty until it is decided), which release/export_tree.py --public applies to its copies.

chosen.about: The decided public name, empty (null) until it is decided: name (the product name), slug (its lower-case, hyphenated form), holder (the MIT copyright holder; null: '{name} contributors') and families (user-visible families to rewrite besides the defaults: launcher-script, licence-file, layer-description). With a name and slug here, release/export_tree.py --public applies rename.py's user-visible rewrites (the default families plus these) to the exported copies only: this tree keeps the internal names, and the public package.json's name follows package-name's public_template. Compatibility families are not rewritten by the export (rename.py apply --include-compat or --family in an export, deliberately). rename.py chosen_name() checks this block like apply's arguments. Fill it in only with the decided name; a test or trial uses a scratch copy.
chosen.name: FreeFG

public_root_files.about: Files release/export_tree.py --public writes at the top of a public export besides the keep list (export_tree.py PUBLIC_ROOT: copies of packaging/public/ with their links adjusted). rename.py includes them only in a public tree (one without release/keep.txt); the private tree's own README.md is research text.

exclude.release/names.json: this list: its patterns spell every old identifier
exclude.release/test_release_tools.py: the release tools' tests, whose fixtures spell the old identifiers
exclude.packaging/public/check_public_docs.py: the document checker's own list of identifiers that follow the rename (its RENAME and OLD_NAMES patterns): update it by hand after a rename

library_owner.about: The private library owner (outside this tree) deploys only packages whose manifest name ends in private-test-NN and reads their receipt qualification/xemfg-vNN-package.json. apply never changes the private names (package.json 'name' and the private variants): only the public variant's name, which must not match this pattern.

name_rules.about: A product name or slug is refused when one of its words, after splitting at spaces, hyphens, dots, digits and camel-case boundaries, is one of refused_words (case-insensitive): 'Xe Pace', 'XeBoost', 'FSR4 Plus', 'DLSS-lite' and 'Intel Pacer' are refused. Nominative use in the documents ('works with Intel XeSS Frame Generation') is not affected. A refused word inside a longer word ('Xenon', 'Intellect') and the hardware name are warnings.
name_rules.name: ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 .-]{0,38}[A-Za-z0-9]$

warned_patterns.(?i)bc-?250: names the ASRock BC-250 hardware: fine nominatively ('for the BC-250'), but in the product name it reads as ASRock's product

families.current: bc250-fsr4-xemfg-private-test-NN (private, top-level 'name'), -NN-intel-free (private variant), -NN-intel-free-2x (the 0.9.0 public variant), -NN-intel-free-mfg (the public variant since 1.0.0)
families.compatibility: The installer records the package name in state.json for Status only; Restore does not compare it. The private library owner's pattern private-test-(\d+)$ keeps matching the private names, which apply leaves alone; the public variant never matched it (the owner does not deploy it). release/assemble.py accepts the private names as before (version vNN[-variant], receipt qualification/xemfg-vNN[-variant]-package.json) and a name of public_template's form ({slug}: name_rules slug; {number}: a build number, the integer the private builds count, or a dotted semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH such as 0.1.0): its version is 'v' + number + public_template's text after {number} (v31-2x, v0.1.0-2x), its receipt qualification/ + public_receipt_template ({slug}, {version}, {number}: lumen-pace-v31-2x-package.json); a public name the library owner's pattern would match, or whose slug carries a refused word, is refused. The package-name replacement below must produce public_template (rename.py checks it). The version is decided: 1.0.0 (0.9.0 was the private pre-release for review, the 2x-only variant intel-free-2x), written as fixed text in public_template ({slug}-1.0.0) and in the replacement's template (\1{slug}-1.0.0\3), so the package is <slug>-1.0.0 (version v1.0.0, receipt <slug>-v1.0.0-package.json); since 1.0.0 the replacement's pattern names the public variant intel-free-mfg. Before the version was decided, public_template {slug}-{number}-2x kept the private build number (the replacement's \2). A later version is the same two edits, the version as fixed text in place of the old one in public_template and in the replacement's template, the same in both: {slug}-0.1.0 with \1{slug}-0.1.0\3 gives <slug>-0.1.0 (version v0.1.0, receipt <slug>-v0.1.0-package.json); {slug}-0.1.0-2x keeps the 2x suffix (v0.1.0-2x, which semantic versioning reads as a pre-release of 0.1.0); {slug}-32-2x gives v32-2x. Nothing else changes: assemble.py accepts a template with a fixed version (a build number or MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, then text such as -2x), rename.py compares the rewritten name with public_template, and the release tests fix their own copy of this family in the build-number form.
families.recommendation: Rename the public variant (dropping 'intel-free', a mark in a package name); keep every private name. A renamed public tree assembles under the public name (release/assemble.py package_naming()).
